full_judgment: 8. As against the submissions advanced from the side of the learned counsel for the petitioner the learned advocate on behalf of the defendant-opposite parties opposing the Rule submits that the learned Appellate Court committed no illegality or irregularity in deciding the fate of the appeal in favour of the appellants. The learned advocate further submits that all the matters in issue were thoroughly discussed and considered by the learned Court of appeal consulting the evidence on records and after vivid discussions over the findings and decisions of the trial Court the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Comilla during disposal of the appeal reversed the findings of the learned Assistant Judge, Debidar, Comilla on the material issue which is the subject matter of the suit for specific performance of contract. The learned advocate also submits that the main matter in issue in a suit for specific performance of contract under the purview of Section 31 of the Specific Relief Act is such that as to whether there was any contract between the parties in respect of sale of the property and whether there has been any violation of the terms and conditions of such contract or Biana Patro if any whatsoever. If it is found that in fact there was no existence of any contract or Baina Patro in favour of the plaintiff to the original suit and the papers produced is collusive and not acted upon which was not executed by the vendors of the property the suit for specific performance of contract cannot sustain and is liable to be dismissed. The canted advocate lastly submits that the learned Appellate Court below in the impugned judgment and decree although decided the issue Nos. l, 2 and 3 in favour of the plaintiff-petitioner but the main subject matter of the instant suit for specific performance of contract was otherwise decided. The point of limitation, defect of parties and maintainability i.e. the issue Nos. 1-3 of the suit cannot be the deciding factors of the instant nature of suit while the alleged "Baina Ptaro" appears to be a forged document and it is established by cogent tangible evidence that in fact there was not contract of sale between the parties and no execution of any Biana Patro in favour of alleged purchaser of the land.
